notes.title: Mega Man 11 zaps, bounds and powers up on PC today
notes.notes:
You wait literally decades for a decent Mega Man PC port – now the new and shiny Mega Man 11 is out, capping off a nineteen game streak of platform shooters featuring Capcom’s iconic Blue Bomber, assuming you’re counting the Legacy Collections. The first main-line Mega Man game since 2010, this one offers familiar platforming with a modern cel-shaded 3D look and some new options to ease players unused to ‘NES hard’ games into the fun. Oh, and bullet time – check out the launch trailer below.

notes.title: Frame rate issue upon initial boot
notes.notes:
We're looking into an issue where the frame rate performance may suffer upon initial launch when the game fails to acquire the monitor refresh rate information.

While we continue to investigate the matter, you may be able to DIY-fix the issue by editing the RefreshRate option within the Config.ini file by following the steps outlined below.

*Please make sure the game has been fully shut down.
[olist]
[*]Open the "Config" file from the folder below using a text editor such as Windows Notepad:

  [b]Mega Man X Legacy Collection[/b]
　C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Mega Man X Legacy Collection\

 [b]Mega Man X Legacy Collection 2[/b]
　C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Mega Man X Legacy Collection 2\

Note the directory above is the default location.  The path may differ if you changed the drive letter or manually modified the game install location.

[*] If you see "RefreshRate=Unknown", change it to "RefreshRate=60.00Hz" and save the file.

[*] Launch the game and verify performance[/olist]
Once again, our sincere apologies for the inconvenience.

notes.title: Patch Notes (Sept. 5th, 2018)
notes.notes:
A new patch has been deployed today with the following fixes/changes:

- Fixed an issue where the game may crash when connected to a high refresh rate monitor.

- There were instances where the game did not function correctly when connected to a high refresh rate monitor that offers numerous resolution options.  This has now been addressed.

This patch should improve or eliminate stability or launch issues that were dependent on the connected display device.

notes.title: Mega Man X Legacy Collection 1 + 2 Patch Now Available
notes.notes:
Hey there fellow Maverick Hunters,

A new patch has been made available for [i]Mega Man X Legacy Collection[/i] and [i]Mega Man X Legacy Collection 2[/i] which provides the following updates:

[list]
[*]To address the screen blackout that affected some users when launching the game, the game now checks the resolution of the connected display device and supported resolutions and sets the appropriate output resolution accordingly
[*]Added V-Sync ON/OFF toggle. This option can be found under Options > Graphics > V-Sync. Turning off V-Sync may help increase performance if users experience framerate issues
[/list]

Thanks again for your patience and support and enjoy!

Best Regards,

Capcom USA Customer Support

notes.title: Capcom s 8-game Mega Man X Legacy Collection is out now
notes.notes:
For the first time, Capcom’s entire Mega Man X series of platform shooters is available on PC. ‘X’ may live in a slightly darker world than his smaller, cuter predecessor Mega Man, but these are still games about a heroic blue robot running around, collecting new weaponry and equipment and shooting stuff with energy bolts that look like lemons. General save-the-world stuff, time and time again. Eight times, in fact. The Mega Man X Legacy Collection (broken up into two releases featuring X1-X4, and X5-X8) is out now, having launched on Tuesday.

(more…)

notes.title: Mega Man X Legacy Collections axe Axel (and the rest of Guns N Roses)
notes.notes:
Nineties platformer icons are a recurring theme this summer. While the return of Crash Bandicoot doesn’t exactly set my heart ablaze, I am entirely down with the entire 8-game Mega Man X series coming to PC, bringing us generations worth of grim anime platform robo-murder all in one place.

The two compilations now have a Steam store page and a price-tag to accompany earlier news of some interesting new playmodes, along with news that Mega Man X5’s bizarre English-only Guns N’ Roses references have been cut.
